rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 7-8 and Table F.3 report the authors' own experiment training a fine-tuned VGG16 with a new fully connected layer on a Mendeley tomato-pest image dataset (4263 images, 8 pest classes), reaching 96.5% test accuracy versus SGD/RMSProp/Adam variants and custom VGG16.
rows.notes: The paper is predominantly a survey, but it contains one primary component: an image-classification experiment for tomato pest detection. That experiment does not test remote sensing, does not address weeds, and does not measure herbicide use or environmental effect; it only reports classification accuracy and loss. The weed-detection material (Yu et al. 2019, Bah et al. 2018, Huang et al. 2020 on UAV weed mapping and precision spraying) is reviewed from other work, not the authors' own result, so it does not count. The statement that precise spraying reduces herbicides (Section 2.3) is an unsupported assertion in the review text. The own result (pest detection) is at most a precondition for targeted pesticide application, not evidence of reduced herbicide use; hence upstream = true, and the technology (ground-image DL pest classification) differs from the remote sensing of weeds named in the passage, hence technology_mismatch = true.

notes: Survey paper with an appended primary experiment (DL pest classification). Full text appears complete. Accuracy figures are inconsistently reported (96.58%, 94.6%, 94.8%, 96.5%) across the abstract, introduction and results, but this does not affect the rating since the claim is not supported by the study's own evidence.
